title: UAP secrecy justified under a law enforcement provision

tellings.quote: he noticed that they are justifying secrecy under a law enforcement provision rather than just National Security

The DoD organization, AARO, has been labeling many documents with a B7 exemption, which Greenewald says does not make any sense. They are stating that anything AARO does is involved in a law enforcement investigation, which allows AARO to not release it.

plain: The Pentagon office that studies UAP, the government's term for UFOs, is said to be keeping its files secret by calling them law-enforcement matters instead of national security ones. The journalist Michael Shellenberger, citing the records researcher John Greenewald Jr., told Michels this, and he also put it in his written statement to a hearing of the House Oversight Committee, "Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Exposing the Truth", on 13 November 2024: the office, AARO, "has been labeling many documents with a B7 exemption", the law-enforcement exception in FOIA, the US law that lets anyone request government records, so that "anything AARO does is involved in a law enforcement investigation, which allows AARO to not release it." The statement reports what Greenewald noticed and his view that it "does not make any sense"; why the office chose that label, it does not say.
